newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes start week steady, outrights fall.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes start week steady, outrights fall.

text.p: U.S. cash crude grades began the week in steady fashion, while outright crude values retreated from sharp Friday advances.
Market volumes were thinned by the fact many players were attending the annual National Petroleum Refiners Association meeting in San Antonio, Texas, which runs through Tuesday.
Price direction was forecast lower by one Texas trader, who noted the narrow April/May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing spread indicated a soft market.
Currently, the Apr WTI was around 30 cts lower at $20.95-21.05, with the May only 3-5 cts higher.
"The spread tells you how the market really is," noted one trader, who believed a contango Apr/May was in the offing.
For the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was talked at WTI/Cushing minus 14-17 cts, a shade firmer than late talk Friday.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire came in at WTI/Cushing -40 cts on the offer side, with bids scarcely seen.
Midland/WTI rounded out the key sweet grades at a 28-35 cts discount to the WTI/Cushing, steady from last deals recorded.
Sour grades were steady in the West Texas Sour/Midland at a $2.58-60 discount to the WTI/Cushing, and Eugene Island barely moved from Friday at WTI/Cushing minus $2.40-50.
